title: The wager — twenty thousand at Baring's
learning_goal: Know the fictional trigger, the six names, £20,000 at Baring's, and the deadline; feel the click of a plan.

narration.script: Evening, at the whist table. In the novel — and only in the novel — a gentleman has walked out of the Bank of England three days ago with fifty-five thousand pounds, and the Daily Telegraph has printed a timetable showing the world can be circled in eighty days. Andrew Stuart, an engineer, wagers four thousand pounds that it cannot be done. Fogg raises him: twenty thousand pounds, on deposit at Baring's — half his fortune — in 'eighty days or less; in nineteen hundred and twenty hours, or a hundred and fifteen thousand two hundred minutes'. Look at the card: six names on the memorandum — Stuart first, Fogg last. Due back 'in this very room of the Reform Club, on Saturday, the 21st of December, at a quarter before nine p.m.' Verne's arithmetic holds: it is exactly eighty days, and it really was a Saturday. Fogg's motto for the evening: 'The unforeseen does not exist.' One footnote from today. Baring's, Fogg's bank, was one of London's oldest; it went under in 1995. The wager has outlived the bank.
